intervals.label: e+e- collider operation (VEPP-4 and VEPP-4M)
intervals.locator: Skrinsky (PAC 1995), section 1.5; the KEDR home page records KEDR experiments at VEPP-4M since 2002
intervals.note: Skrinsky dates the VEPP-4 collider operation from 1980 (maximum 5.5 GeV per beam then); the VEPP-4M upgrade date was not found in the sources fetched. KEDR has taken data at VEPP-4M since 2002 and published new results in 2025 (arXiv:2506.02421).
intervals.quote: Since 1980 the higher energy e+e- collider VEPP-4 is in operation at Novosibirsk

name: VEPP-4M
notes: The VEPP-4 to VEPP-4M upgrade date is not stated in the sources fetched; the record starts at the VEPP-4 start (1980).

beam_energy.note: The page says the VEPP-4 complex includes the VEPP-4M e+e- collider up to 6 GeV; the KEDR page quotes a total range 2E = 2-11 GeV.

summary.plain: The high-energy electron-positron collider of the Budker Institute in Novosibirsk, Siberia, which reaches up to 6 GeV per beam. Its KEDR detector has measured the J/psi, psi(2S) and tau masses with record precision, using a very accurate beam-energy calibration.
summary.technical: VEPP-4M e⁺e⁻ collider (VEPP-4 complex with the VEPP-3 storage ring and an injector): up to 6 GeV per beam; precise beam-energy measurement by resonant depolarisation (about 10⁻⁷ relative accuracy) and Compton backscattering; operating since 1980 as VEPP-4; KEDR experiments since 2002.
